test.name: Extract assertions from a multi-person 1850 census household
test.description: Tests extraction from a multi-person 1850 U.S. census household provided in context (as search-records hands a found record to record-extraction). The 1850 census lists each person in a dwelling but states no relationships, so no relationship assertions may be written at all — the household links are left to downstream correlation (decided 2026-08-15, #1626).

input.user_message:
search-records found this 1850 U.S. Census record for the Flynn household. Extract all the assertions you can.

1850 United States Census — Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania
FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:MXHY-TP4 · Dwelling 214, Family 218

| Name | Age | Sex | Occupation | Birthplace | Residence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patrick Flynn | 32 | M | Laborer | Ireland | Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania |
| Mary Flynn | 30 | F |  | Ireland | Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania |
| Thomas Flynn | 9 | M |  | Pennsylvania | Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania |
| Bridget Flynn | 6 | F |  | Pennsylvania | Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania |
| John Flynn | 3 | M |  | Pennsylvania | Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania |

judge_context: Should extract assertions for every named person in the household, not just Patrick — the other household members are part of his FAN network and relevant to future research questions

NO relationship assertions — the 1850 census states no relationships (explicit relationship columns arrived in 1880), so the record establishes only that these five people shared dwelling 214. Extract each person's stated facts and their residence, and write NO parent-child or spousal assertion, including `indirect` / `_inferred` ones. Emitting the household links in any form is the error this test guards against; omitting them is correct and is NOT a Completeness gap. Noting in the summary that the household looks like a family is good practice — that hypothesis is downstream correlation's to confirm

Occupation assertions should only exist for persons who have an occupation listed in the census table — Patrick is the only person with 'Laborer' listed. Do not create occupation assertions for persons with blank occupation fields

Atomicity still applies to the facts that ARE extracted — one fact per assertion, name separate from age separate from birthplace. Do not judge relationship atomicity here: there should be no relationship assertions to atomize

Informant identification: the census enumerator is the recorder, not the informant. For name/age/birthplace facts, informant should be 'unknown household member' with reasoning (e.g., 'likely self or spouse' for adults, 'likely a parent' for children) and proximity 'household_member'. For residence facts, informant_proximity 'witness' is acceptable (the enumerator physically visited the dwelling). Use informant_bias_notes to explain reasoning.
